chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever kills himself intentionally, he is in the Hellfire, 'abiding eternally therein'.' I said to him: 'What do you think if he made a will and then killed himself immediately? Will his will be executed?' He said: 'If he made a will before an event occurred in himself from a wound or killing, his will is accepted in his third, and if he made a will after he occurred in himself from a wound or killing, perhaps he will die, his will is not accepted.'.
ai.seo_question: Does a suicide victim's will remain valid according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that intentional suicide results in eternal abode in Hellfire, while the validity of the deceased's will hinges on the timing relative to the onset of the fatal condition. If the will was made before the injury or death occurred, it is accepted for one-third of the estate; however, if made after the fatal act, it is generally rejected, reflecting the juristic principle that the 'event' (hadath) invalidates subsequent dispositions. This distinction highlights the Shia legal focus on the state of mind and physical condition at the moment of testamentary intent.
